writeup: TIC 367000921 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.2401 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing a 4.64 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was observed. The eclipse signal achieved a detection significance of 1399.9 in the BLS periodogram analysis, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 93.6. The measured centroid offset of 0.8 arcsec from the target location is consistent with the target star itself. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel detection. The machine-learning screening algorithm assigned it a score of 0.92, indicating high confidence that this represents a real eclipsing system rather than an instrumental artifact or false positive.
